question.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{n}^{3}(5x+10)^{n}=(5x+10)+{2}^{3}(5x+10)^{2}+{3}^{3}(5x+10)^{3}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}={n}^{3}(5x+10)^{n}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{3}(5x+10)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}(5x+10)^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(n+1)^{3}(5x+10)}{{n}^{3}}| \\  & =|5x+10|{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n+1}{n})}^{3} \\  & =|5x+10|\cdot 1 \\  & =5|x+2|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if $|x+2|<\frac{1}{5}.$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\frac{1}{5}.$
